title: Indian-Origin Surrey Landlady Arrested After Tenant's Viral Harassment Videos
excerpt: Raj Tiwana was taken into custody by Surrey Police after a tenant documented alleged harassment, unauthorized entries, and physical confrontations in videos that spread widely online. Police have issued no official statement, and the exact charges remain unclear.
body:
• Surrey Police took Indian-origin landlady Raj Tiwana into custody after her tenant posted videos alleging harassment, unauthorized entry, and physical confrontations at the rental property.
  • The footage, shared on an Instagram account called "Tiwana Farm Survivor," shows disputes that began with a barbecue grill and escalated into allegations of rock-throwing, changed locks, and a disrupted power supply.
  • Neither the full context nor the authenticity of the videos has been independently verified, and police have issued no official statement on the arrest or any charges.
  • The incident has ignited debate among diaspora communities about landlords' obligations and tenants' legal protections under British Columbia law.

A Dispute That Turned Into an Arrest

A landlord-tenant dispute in Surrey, British Columbia, exploded into public view this week after a tenant began documenting his clashes with his landlady on Instagram — footage that ended with Surrey Police taking the woman into custody in front of the camera.

https://x.com/yegwave/status/2098908680229916778

The woman, identified by the tenant as Raj Tiwana, an Indian national, was arrested after the tenant shared a series of videos alleging that she repeatedly interfered with his use of the property, entered his rental unit without permission, and became involved in physical confrontations, according to American Bazaar Online. In the final clip, officers can be seen telling Tiwana she was under arrest. She appears surprised and asks whether she can call her daughter before officers handcuff her and escort her to a police vehicle.

The exact charges against Tiwana, and the circumstances surrounding her arrest, were not immediately available. Police have issued no official statement on the incident.

From a Barbecue to Changed Locks

The videos were posted on an Instagram account called "Tiwana Farm Survivor" and have since attracted widespread attention on social media, with many prominent accounts in Canada and India sharing them. According to a Times of India report cited by American Bazaar Online, the dispute began when the tenant, who said he was 50, was preparing food on a barbecue outside the rental property with a friend.

In one video, Tiwana can be seen objecting to the barbecue, pointing toward brown marks on a wall and raising concerns about damage to the property. The tenant responds that the marks are rust and argues that he has the right to have a friend over because he pays rent, while his friend records the confrontation on a mobile phone.

"I am 50 years old. I can have my friend over for dinner and I pay rent."

— The tenant, in one of the viral videos

The disagreement then escalated over the food itself. In another clip, Tiwana is seen removing food from the barbecue while the tenant and his friend are preparing dinner. According to the tenant's account, she picked up a piece of wood and pushed the food off the grill, saying she could not allow them to cook on the property. The tenant accused his landlady of trying to intimidate them, while she reportedly threatened to call the police and suggested he could go to his friend's home if he wanted to have a barbecue.

What began as an argument over a grill soon widened into a broader dispute over the tenant's use of the property. In subsequent videos, the tenant alleged that Tiwana entered his home without permission and repeatedly interfered with his access to the unit. One clip appears to show her entering the rental space while the tenant repeatedly asks her to leave. Another video reportedly shows Tiwana throwing rocks in the tenant's direction before a physical confrontation, and in a separate clip she appears to grab a container from a table and strike the tenant's friend while questioning his presence at the property.

The tenant also claimed that Tiwana entered his home while he was away and later changed the locks. He said his rent had been paid through August 15 and alleged that the entrance to his rental unit had been left without a door. In another video, he claimed the property had been broken into for the third time and that the door had been completely removed. He further alleged that she switched off his power intentionally.

What Tenancy Law Says

Under British Columbia's Residential Tenancy Act, landlords generally cannot enter a tenant's rental unit without giving proper written notice except in emergencies, and they cannot cut off or interfere with essential services like power. Changing locks without the tenant's consent and entering a home while the tenant is away are the kinds of actions tenants can challenge through the Residential Tenancy Branch's dispute-resolution process.

The viral case has also drawn attention to a practical gap: many immigrant landlords carry over property norms from home, where owners exercise broad control over their premises. In Canada, those expectations run into strict tenant protections — and trying to enforce house rules through confrontation, as the footage appears to show, can end in criminal liability rather than compliance.

Some social media users claimed they had also stayed on the same property and faced similar treatment from the woman, though those accounts have not been verified.

Diaspora Angle

For Indian-origin landlords in Canada, the case is a cautionary reminder that property disputes must be handled through provincial tenancy law — written notices, documented complaints, and the Residential Tenancy Branch — not personal confrontation, regardless of cultural expectations around how a property should be used.

What's Next

Whether formal charges will be laid remains unclear, and the Surrey Police have yet to issue a statement. The videos' full context and authenticity have not been independently verified, and Tiwana's account of the dispute has not been publicly heard. If charges follow, the case could become a closely watched test of how quickly viral documentation of tenant grievances moves from social media outrage to legal process.
image_caption: Two Surrey Police officers escort a handcuffed woman outside a house in Surrey, British Columbia. The woman is Raj Tiwana, the Indian-origin landlady taken into custody after her tenant posted viral videos alleging harassment and unauthorized entry at the rental property.
